entry.title: OpenAI shares ten new AI-generated results solving long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI announced ten new results addressing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, achieved using an internal version of its Astra model. These results cover areas including high-dimensional geometry, coding theory, group theory, quantum complexity, and lattice cryptography, with proofs formalized in Lean and manuscripts prepared with human assistance. The work builds on a previous AI-generated disproof of the Erdős unit-distance conjecture and aims to empower researchers by providing tools that accelerate discovery. OpenAI emphasizes responsible attribution, acknowledging the AI system's role in generating the arguments while taking responsibility for their correctness, and encourages the mathematical community to engage with and build upon these findings.

entry.title: YC Software launches qm, a multiplayer AI agent platform for startups with isolated and shared workspaces in Slack and web [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: YC Software has released qm, an open-source multiplayer AI agent platform designed for startups that allows employees to work independently or collaboratively within Slack and web environments. Each user and channel has isolated memory, files, permissions, and tools, enabling personalized and shared workflows without interference. The platform supports multiple AI models and harnesses, including Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code, and offers features like admin controls, custom internal web apps, shared skills, and background task scheduling. QM emphasizes security with configurable approval workflows and content screening, and deployments run in an organization's own cloud environment with customizable infrastructure and policies.

entry.title: Aurora launches a self-hosted AI gateway in Go supporting 14 providers including OpenAI and Anthropic with unified API routing and caching [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Aurora is a self-hosted AI gateway built in Go that provides a single API interface compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, enabling apps to route requests to 14 different AI providers without code changes. It supports features like provider auto-discovery, load balancing, model aliasing, failover, and configurable workflows for routing, caching, and guardrails. The gateway offers extensive caching options including exact and semantic caches, security features such as rate limiting, PII redaction, prompt injection blocking, and system prompt protection. It also includes observability tools like audit logging, usage analytics, Prometheus metrics, and an admin dashboard for managing providers, keys, and workflows.

entry.summary: Granola, a startup founded in 2023 and valued at $1.5 billion, offers an AI-powered app that records meetings, generates notes, and suggests follow-ups, integrating seamlessly with platforms like Zoom and Google Meet. Its recent Apple Watch app release has revitalized interest in the device, with users praising its unobtrusive recording and ease of use compared to existing solutions. The app's popularity has grown steadily, expanding its staff and office space, and attracting attention from notable users. Apple could benefit from acquiring Granola to inject innovation into its product lineup, especially as it develops new AI wearables and smart glasses. Granola's focus on simplicity and user engagement aligns with Apple's product philosophy, and the acquisition would fit Apple's preference for smaller, strategic purchases rather than mega-acquisitions.

entry.title: DSCode launches an open source coding agent powered by DeepSeek for local repository editing, testing, and review with sandboxed tools and cost tracking [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: DSCode is an open source coding agent built around DeepSeek that enables developers to plan, edit, test, and review code directly from the terminal within real repositories. It supports local sessions stored as JSONL files, runs commands in an OS sandbox with networking blocked by default, and tracks token usage and estimated costs. The tool allows parallel agents to handle multiple tasks concurrently and integrates with existing repository workflows without vendor lock-in or hidden telemetry. Installation requires Node.js 22.19+ and Git, and users can connect DSCode to DeepSeek via an API key or compatible gateway. The project emphasizes local control, transparency, and extensibility, offering a cost-aware and secure environment for coding tasks. DSCode is available globally via npm and is licensed under MIT.

entry.title: Wienerdog launches open-source tool adding file-based memory and self-improving skills for Claude Code and Codex AI agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Wienerdog is an open-source tool that enhances AI agents Claude Code and Codex by providing them with persistent memory, habits, and daily routines using only local files. It operates without servers or telemetry, storing data on the user's machine in a shared memory vault accessible by both agents, enabling continuity across sessions and tools. The tool includes features like an AI-generated profile, a markdown memory vault structured for compatibility with Obsidian, and a nightly "dreaming" process that reviews conversations to promote important information into long-term memory and develop reusable skills. Installation is supported on macOS, Linux, and Windows, with scripts that handle dependencies and setup, and users can verify the installation plan before proceeding. Wienerdog is actively maintained and considered in early development stages, with file formats subject to change until version 1.0.

entry.title: Researchers introduce AISPA, a user-centric framework auditing system prompts in 88 commercial AI products across eight user-relevant dimensions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AISPA is a framework designed to systematically audit system prompts that guide foundation models in AI applications, focusing on user-centric evaluation to address trust and accountability gaps. The researchers analyzed 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products, classifying them as protective or problematic based on eight dimensions important to users. Their audit revealed significant variation in prompt design, widespread but shallow adoption of protective instructions, increasing prompt length and user protection over time, and the persistent presence of problematic instructions in about 40% of products. The findings underscore the need for greater transparency, standardization, and independent oversight of system prompts in commercial AI systems.

entry.title: Publishers withdraw debut novel 'Call Me, I'll Hide the Body' amid AI authorship concerns, jeopardizing book and film rights deals [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The debut novel 'Call Me, I'll Hide the Body' faced a major setback when publishers and film rights buyers pulled back due to questions about the use of AI in its creation. The author had initially assured that AI was not involved, but suspicions arose during the rights selling process, leading to withdrawal of the book from international submissions and halting momentum for its adaptation. The novel had secured a $2.4 million deal with Minotaur/Macmillan and attracted significant interest for film and TV adaptations. However, concerns about AI involvement raised issues around copyright registration and clear title chains, complicating the publishing and entertainment industry's ability to proceed. This incident highlights growing challenges for authors and rights holders regarding AI's role in creative works and its impact on intellectual property rights.

entry.title: Report: Enterprises are prematurely adopting AI and projecting transformation without foundational readiness, risking technical and financial debt [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article compares enterprises' current AI adoption strategies to the 'Anna Delvey' approach of faking success, highlighting how companies spend heavily and showcase AI initiatives to stakeholders without building the necessary underlying capabilities. This leads to accumulating technical, financial, and credibility debts as the initial appearances of transformation fail to deliver real returns. It explains that enterprises often announce ambitious AI projects, reallocate resources to flashy pilots, and integrate AI into workflows without clear business outcomes or proper risk assessments. The pressure to appear transformed drives this behavior, but the resulting debts-both explicit and implicit-pose long-term challenges that will require significant effort to resolve.

entry.title: OpenAI's GPT 5.6 Pro solves longstanding math problems including the Unit Distance Conjecture, prompting mixed reactions from mathematicians [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's GPT 5.6 Pro has recently solved significant mathematical problems, such as disproving the Unit Distance Conjecture, a challenge open since 1946. This breakthrough has sparked varied responses in the mathematical community, with some embracing AI as a productivity tool while others express concern about its impact on mathematical culture and expertise. Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers noted that GPT 5.6 Pro solved two problems he had worked on extensively in a single attempt, which he found unsettling despite appreciating the solutions. He worries that increased reliance on AI could lead to a loss of deep human understanding in mathematics, even as many researchers advocate for transparency and responsible AI use in the field through initiatives like the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics.

entry.title: Schmitech launches ORBIT, an open-source AI platform providing a unified OpenAI-compatible API for connecting private data, models, and tools with built-in authentication and governance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: ORBIT is an open-source backend API platform that enables users to connect files, databases, vector stores, models, APIs, and tools through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It supports local or cloud deployment with features like authentication, observability, and governance, allowing seamless transition from prototypes to production environments without changing architecture. The platform includes a web UI for chat and document interaction, supports multiple AI models including local and cloud-based options, and offers an admin panel for managing adapters and configurations. ORBIT is designed to serve as an AI gateway combining retrieval and tool execution, with production controls integrated rather than relying on application code. It is actively maintained and available via Docker images for quick setup and experimentation.

entry.title: OpenAI and partners report AI coding agents can modernize research software with up to 60x speedups but cannot reliably verify scientific correctness [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A field report from OpenAI and academic collaborators shows that AI coding agents can significantly update and accelerate aging research software, achieving speed improvements of up to 60 times. However, these agents often produce code that is confidently incorrect, shifting the challenge from coding to verifying scientific validity. The report covers eight case studies, mainly in biology, where agents like Codex and Claude Code performed tasks ranging from maintenance to full rewrites in modern languages. While the agents handled implementation, human researchers defined goals and validation methods, as the AI systems could not reliably judge the scientific accuracy of their outputs. This highlights the ongoing need for expert oversight despite advances in AI-assisted coding.

entry.title: Researcher demonstrates self-spreading worm in Word documents exploiting Microsoft Copilot prompt injections, Microsoft confirms but has not fixed issue after 144 days [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: A security researcher has demonstrated a worm-like attack that hides invisible prompt injections inside Microsoft Word documents, which hijack Microsoft Copilot by spreading automatically into new files each time they are reused. Microsoft confirmed the vulnerability on March 31 but has failed to fix it after two attempts and 144 days. The attack uses white text on a white background at tiny font size, which Copilot processes but users cannot see, allowing the malicious instructions to propagate when documents are used as templates or sources. The researcher, Håkon Måløy, published his findings without revealing the payload text due to the lack of a fix. This vulnerability highlights ongoing challenges with prompt injection attacks in AI systems, which remain an unresolved security problem. The issue could allow compromised documents, such as market analyses, to manipulate subsequent reports by spreading the hidden instructions through Copilot's processing.
